A founder of the PAIGC with Amilcar Cabral, who became the first president of Cape Verde at independence on 5 July 1975.

After Cabral's murder in 1973 he led the party. The plan was a union of Cape Verde and Guinea-Bissau, but after the 1980 coup in Bissau the Cape Verdean branch broke away as its own party. Pereira ruled a one-party state, careful and fairly mild, that depended on food aid. In 1990 he accepted multiparty rule, and in the 1991 elections his party lost. He handed over power peacefully.
